description: CSE students and space enthusiasts building an immersive storytelling experience for NASA Space Apps 2026. Looking for teammates skilled in UI/UX, frontend, 3D/WebGL, research, storytelling, data visualization, and design. Let’s aim for Global Winner!
summary:
"Still Here" is an interactive, bilingual (English/Bengali) space museum built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, "Abandoned but not Forgotten," and aimed at learners aged 8-16. It tells the stories of six pieces of NASA hardware that were retired, went silent, or were left behind: the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, the rovers Opportunity, Spirit and Sojourner, the Phoenix lander and Pioneer 10. Each has a four-chapter story, sourced NASA facts, a Last Signal timeline, a planned-versus-actual Mission Clock and 3D/AR models.

The app also includes a grounded AI explorer that only repeats verified facts, a three-mission Mars rover game, cinema-mode films, quizzes with badges, an interactive timeline, a live Pioneer 10 tracker and historic Apollo 11 audio. It is a fully static React, TypeScript and Three.js site with no accounts or tracking.
details:
Still Here - Their Missions Ended. Their Stories Live On.

Project by Team Niharika | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Challenge: Abandoned but not Forgotten

Project Description

Still Here is an interactive, bilingual (English/Bangla) space museum designed to bring the stories of forgotten, retired, silent and left-behind space exploration hardware back to life. Developed for learners aged 8–16, the project transforms the history of space exploration into an immersive educational experience where children can explore spacecraft, discover scientific achievements, listen to mission stories, interact with AI-powered explorers, and experience a simulated Mars rover mission.

Space exploration does not end when a mission loses contact or a spacecraft retires. The machines that once explored distant worlds leave behind extraordinary discoveries and stories worth remembering. However, much of this history remains scattered across technical documents and scientific websites that can be difficult for younger audiences to understand. Still Here addresses this gap by turning complex mission histories into an accessible, interactive, and engaging digital experience.

Our museum currently features six historic explorers: the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, Opportunity, Spirit, Phoenix, Sojourner, and Pioneer 10. Through their stories, learners can travel from the Moon to Mars and beyond, discovering what these explorers achieved, how their missions ended, and why their contributions still matter.

What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Still Here combines interactive storytelling, 3D visualization, educational gaming, artificial intelligence, and NASA's scientific resources into one web-based platform.

Its key features include:

  • Interactive 3D Solar System: Learners can explore a 3D solar system, visit the Moon and Mars and discover Pioneer 10's journey into deep space. Interactive planetary globes and mission maps show the real landing locations of historic explorers.
  • Explorer Story Engine: Each explorer has a four-chapter story presented in three different ways: Read, Listen, and Explore Facts. Children can learn through storytelling, narrated content, and NASA-sourced information accompanied by real space imagery.
  • AI Explorer – "If This Rover Could Talk": Learners can ask questions directly to their favorite explorers in English or Bengali. Instead of generating potentially inaccurate information, our AI system retrieves relevant facts from a curated, NASA-sourced knowledge base, provides source links, and responds with "I don't know" when the available information does not support an answer.
  • Mars Rover Mission Game: An interactive 3D simulation allows learners to experience three missions: Explore Mars, Find the Water Evidence, and Save the Mission. Through exploration and challenges involving dust storms and solar power, children discover scientific concepts behind real Mars missions.
  • Cinema Mode: Each explorer's history is transformed into an animated, full-screen cinematic experience with multiple scenes, narration, subtitles and captions in English and Bengali.
  • The Last Signal and Mission Clock: Learners can explore the final days of missions and compare planned mission lifetimes with actual operating lifetimes. For example, Opportunity was originally designed for 90 Martian days but operated for approximately 5,111 Martian days.
  • Pioneer 10 Live Tracker: Using NASA JPL Horizons data, the platform presents Pioneer 10's estimated current distance, speed and light-travel time, helping learners understand its extraordinary journey through deep space.
  • Timeline, Quizzes, and Badges: An interactive historical timeline connects missions from 1962 to 2022 with modern exploration initiatives. Quizzes and eight achievement badges encourage continued learning.
  • 3D Models and Augmented Reality: Learners can examine NASA 3D models of historic spacecraft and view supported models in their surroundings using compatible mobile devices.

The platform runs directly in a web browser without requiring installation, registration, or a user account. Learning progress and badges are stored locally on the learner's device.

What Benefits Does It Have?

Still Here offers several educational and technological benefits:

  1. Makes space science accessible: It transforms complicated scientific and engineering information into child-friendly stories, interactive experiences, and games.
  2. Preserves space exploration history: It gives retired and silent spacecraft a digital place where their missions and discoveries can continue to inspire future generations.
  3. Supports different learning styles: Children can read, listen, watch, explore 3D environments, ask questions, and learn through interactive simulations.
  4. Breaks language barriers: The entire experience, including stories, interface, facts, quizzes, games and AI interaction, is available in both English and Bengali.
  5. Encourages scientific curiosity: Interactive exploration allows learners to understand planetary science, robotics, engineering, communication and the challenges of space missions.
  6. Promotes reliable learning: Every curated fact is connected to a NASA source, while the AI Explorer is designed to avoid unsupported answers.
  7. Provides accessible technology: Lightweight graphics options, responsive layouts, optional narration, captions, and keyboard-friendly controls make the experience usable across different devices and learning environments.

What Is the Intended Impact?

Our primary goal is to make sure that no extraordinary space mission is forgotten simply because its spacecraft has stopped communicating or its mission has officially ended.

We want to inspire children to look beyond the launch of a spacecraft and discover the complete story of exploration: the challenges, discoveries, unexpected achievements, final signals, and lasting scientific contributions.

We also aim to make space education more inclusive, particularly for Bengali-speaking students who may not have access to engaging space-science resources in their native language.

By connecting historic missions with present and future exploration programs such as Artemis, Perseverance, and Voyager, Still Here demonstrates that every mission contributes to humanity's continuing journey of discovery.

Ultimately, we hope to create a growing digital archive of exploration hardware that educators, students, and space enthusiasts can use to learn, remember, and become inspired by the machines that helped humanity understand the universe.

What Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware and Software Did We Use?

Still Here was developed as a modern, static web application using the following technologies:

Programming Languages and Frameworks

  • TypeScript with strict typing
  • HTML5 and CSS3
  • React 18
  • React Router 6
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Node.js scripts

3D Graphics and Interactive Technologies

  • Three.js for 3D environments, planetary globes, and the Mars rover simulation
  • Google Model Viewer for interactive 3D models and augmented reality
  • Draco-compressed GLB models
  • Web Audio API for procedural sound effects and soundscapes
  • Web Speech API for English and Bengali narration

APIs and NASA Resources

  • NASA JPL Horizons API for Pioneer 10 tracking data
  • NASA Image and Video Library API for authentic space imagery
  • NASA 3D Resources for spacecraft models
  • NASA audio archives for historic Apollo 11 recordings
  • NASA Science, NASA JPL, NASA.gov, and NSSDC resources for mission information and fact verification

Development and Deployment Tools

  • Vite 5 for development and production builds
  • Vitest for automated testing
  • ESLint and Prettier for code quality
  • Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration
  • GitHub Actions for automated testing and deployment
  • GitHub Pages for hosting

Hardware: No specialized hardware was required. Development was carried out using ordinary computers and laptops. The application is designed for modern smartphones, tablets, and computers, while augmented reality requires a compatible mobile device.

The application currently operates without a dedicated backend. Its content, AI fact retrieval, interactive experiences, and learning progress run in the browser.

How Is the Project Creative and Innovative?

The most creative aspect of Still Here is its approach to telling the stories of machines rather than simply presenting information about them.

Instead of treating retired spacecraft as outdated equipment, we give each explorer a storytelling identity. Children can experience a mission from the explorer's imagined first-person perspective, while clearly distinguishing creative storytelling from verified scientific facts.

We combine several experiences that are usually found separately into one educational platform: a digital museum, interactive 3D space environment, animated cinema, educational game, AI-powered question-answering system, and augmented reality viewer.

Another important innovation is our approach to trustworthy AI in education. Rather than allowing an AI model to invent answers, our current AI Explorer retrieves information directly from verified facts and provides the original NASA sources. This makes accuracy and transparency more important than simply producing a conversational response.

Our full Bengali localization is also a major part of the innovation. Bengali is not just an additional interface translation; it is supported throughout the stories, narration, quizzes, games, and AI question-answering experience.

Finally, procedural graphics and audio generation allow us to create immersive experiences directly through code while keeping the application relatively lightweight and accessible.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

Throughout development, we considered several important factors:

1. Scientific Accuracy and Reliability: Every curated fact is connected to a NASA source. We implemented a fact-checking process in which another team member reviews the original source before a fact is marked verified. Imaginative storytelling, artistic representations, and simplified simulations are clearly labelled.

2. Age-Appropriate Education: Since our primary audience is children aged 8–16, we designed short story chapters, simple explanations, intuitive navigation, visual guidance, interactive challenges, and rewarding learning experiences.

3. Language and Inclusion: We developed complete English and Bengali experiences, including translated stories, facts, games, quizzes, subtitles, and narration. We also considered keyboard accessibility and readable interfaces.

4. Privacy and Safety: The platform does not require accounts, sign-ups, cookies, or analytics. Learning progress stays in the browser. The AI Explorer cannot freely generate unsupported responses, helping keep educational content controlled and age-appropriate.

5. Performance and Device Compatibility: We considered users with different devices and internet capabilities. Lazy-loaded pages, compressed 3D models, procedural assets, responsive layouts, and automatic High/Light graphics settings help the application work on smartphones and less powerful computers.

6. Reliability and Offline Support: We included fallback data for the Pioneer 10 tracker and designed the core experience to work without continuous access to NASA services. NASA photos and other network-dependent resources require connectivity.

7. Scalability and Future Development: The content architecture is designed to support additional explorers, missions, and languages without rebuilding the entire platform. The current browser-based AI retrieval system also has an integration path for a future Python FastAPI and RAG-based backend.

8. Ethical Representation: We clearly distinguish real scientific information from imagined storytelling and artistic interpretation. We also acknowledge the use of AI coding assistance and state that Still Here is an independent student project, not an officially NASA-endorsed product.

Our Vision

Still Here is more than a collection of old spacecraft information. It is an attempt to preserve humanity's exploration legacy and make it meaningful to the next generation.

A rover may stop moving. A spacecraft may go silent. A mission may officially end. But the discoveries, knowledge, and inspiration they leave behind should never disappear.

Their missions ended. Their stories live on.

Built with curiosity by Team Niharika for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Abandoned but not Forgotten.
